The day began with the practical wisdom that only reveals itself after it is too late: if you are going to hike **Mount Vesuvius**, you ought to bring along the hiking poles you packed and carried all the way to Europe for precisely such a purpose. A small lesson in logistics, paid for on volcanic gravel.

The main business of the day was the confirmed **Mount Vesuvius and Herculaneum** trip from Naples, the sort of itinerary that pairs the catastrophe with its source: first the city preserved by the eruption, then the volcano itself above the bay. More details still need to be added as the day fills in.

Food notes are beginning to collect as well: **CROCCANTI**, and pizza at **10 Diego** — specifically **PARIGINA**. There will be a picture, which is good, because some things should be documented visually before anyone tries to improve them with prose.

## Retrospective Notes — Partial

- **Theme so far:** Vesuvius hiking logistics, and the folly of packing useful gear without actually bringing it to the mountain.
- **Packed-but-not-used item:** Hiking poles traveled all the way to Europe but did not make the Vesuvius hike.
- **Planned day:** Herculaneum and Mount Vesuvius tour from Naples.
- **Food note:** CROCCANTI.
- **Pizza note:** 10 Diego — PARIGINA.
